text: Archibald, meet mappity. It's a map you can just talk to.
A talking map. Marvellous. Does it also do my taxes?
Watch. My kid is melting down, and needs sugar, immediately.
Every place you see just answered, with a probability. Four hundred judgments, about a second, a fraction of a cent.
Four hundred opinions in one second. Like my family, but useful.
On the left: Needle, a tiny local model, thought sugar was a landmark. Jev gave that one percent. Overruled.
They mark each other's homework. I approve.
Next. Cozy coffee, within five minutes' walk of the aquarium.
Needle pulls out the aquarium, and the five minutes. Code does the geography. Jev decides what cozy means.
One that no category can answer. Somewhere I'd feel fine walking to, alone, at eleven at night.
Jev decided the street matters, so we asked Mapillary what its cameras saw. Each place is judged twice, itself and its street, and code multiplies the two.
So those little specks are actual lamp posts. Good heavens.
Very worthy. But can it do anything frivolous?
Let's play a guessing game. It's now thinking of one of these sixty places.
Can I eat there?
I only hear one answer. But every place answered, so the odds shift across the whole map. Does it serve alcohol?
Bayes' theorem, as a pub quiz. Stand back. I shall guess.
Ha! First try. I should do this professionally.
Hmph. I demand a recount.
Open Street Map, Mapillary, TypeSafe Jev, and Cactus Needle. About a second per question. No chatbot anywhere.
Splendid. Now ask it where one finds a decent cup of tea.
